content.text: The text reviews chronic gastritis, simple gastric ulcer, gastric cancer, gastric hemorrhage, and stomach dilatation. Chronic gastritis causes impaired digestion, burning epigastric discomfort, nausea, mucus vomiting, anemia, and nutritional decline; treatment emphasizes rest, restricted diets, diluents, and cautious medicines. Gastric ulcer commonly produces meal-related localized pain, vomiting, hemorrhage, anemia, perforation, and possible scarring or pyloric stenosis; treatment centers on strict bland nutrition, rest, symptom control, and management of bleeding or perforation. Gastric cancer typically causes progressive anorexia, vomiting, pain, tumor, cachexia, anemia, metastases, and death, with surgery rarely curative. Gastric hemorrhage has diverse causes, especially ulcer, cancer, portal congestion, and vascular disease. Pyloric obstruction or muscular failure may cause gastric dilatation. **Mary moved to the bathroom.**
